# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) magnetic wireless charging standard. It adds a magnet ring that aligns the phone and charger, and it caps at 15W. Apple contributed its MagSafe tech to the standard ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** (also branded "Qi2 25W") is the newer version, launched in July 2025. It has the same magnetic design but delivers about 70% more power, up to 25W. The WPC says that can take a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's brand for its magnetic charging system. It's supported by iPhone 12 and later, except the SE and 16e ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W, so it follows the Qi2.2 standard ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)). "MagSafe-compatible" on a third-party box is only a compatibility claim. Look for the actual Qi2 or Qi2 25W logo, since only certified products can display it.

## What speed you actually get
- **iPhone 12-15:** up to 15W.
- **iPhone 16 and 16 Pro:** up to 22.5W with Apple's charger.
- **iPhone Air:** up to 20W.
- **iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max and 17 series:** up to 25W. This needs a 30W or greater adapter, which is usually sold separately ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **iPhone 17e:** maxes out at 15W, and the 16e has no wireless charging ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).
- **Android:** support is limited. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do Qi2 at 15W, and the 10 Pro XL does Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is "Qi2 Ready" and needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## Bottom line
- On an iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max or 17 series, a Qi2.2 charger is worth it for the 25W speed.
- On an iPhone 12-15, any Qi2 charger tops out at 15W, so you gain nothing from paying for 25W.
- Chargers are backward compatible, so a 25W charger still works at lower speeds on older phones.

## Example products
- [Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m), $49](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m): Qi2 25W certified. Pair it with a 30W adapter.
- [ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Qi2.2 25W stand](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand): $99.99 list, or $82.00 with code PARTNER18. It needs an iPhone 17 series, 16 Pro Max or 16 Plus on iOS 26 for full 25W.
- [Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 power bank](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w): $59.99 list, or $53.99 with code AM52. It gives 25W on iPhone 16-17 (not the 16e) and 15W on iPhone 12-15.
- [ESR HaloLock 15W Qi2 car charger](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost): $39.99 list, or $32.80 with code PARTNER18. It's Qi2 certified at 15W.
- [ESR Magnetic Charging Pad, 15W](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-qi2-mini-wireless-charger-15w): $19.99 list, or $16.40 with code PARTNER18. It's "MagSafe-style," and its page doesn't state Qi2 certification.

The ESR and Baseus links are affiliate links, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy. The Dealectric page also notes the ESR pad's compatibility details are inconsistent, since it lists both "iPhone 13 or later" and "iPhone 12 or later, except 16 models." Check that before buying for a newer iPhone.
